glance: Obesity pharmacotherapy: ribupatide (GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist) cut weight 10.7% to 17.7% at 48 weeks in GEMINI-1 (JAMA); lower-dose CagriSema 1.7 mg and 1.0 mg each gave about 21% loss at 68 weeks (REDEFINE 9).
Finerenone in FSGS (FIND-CKD prespecified analysis): total eGFR slope improved by 1.3 mL/min/1.73 m2/yr and UPCR fell 41% vs placebo.

Coronary PCI: angiography-derived vFFR met noninferiority to wire FFR at 1 year (LIPSIA-STRATEGY); super-high-pressure balloons noninferior to intravascular lithotripsy for stent expansion (VICTORY); DECISION-CTO 10-year data show no difference.

Neutral or negative: upadacitinib in Takayasu arteritis (SELECT-TAK, primary end point missed), prediction-aided bDMARD tapering in RA (PATIO), diabetes-educated psychologist for HbA1c in type 1 diabetes.
MSG-ERC and ECMM published five consensus papers revising clinical trial end points for invasive fungal disease; IPD meta-analysis puts 1-year invasive aspergillosis mortality at 53.8%.
Guidance: ACC scientific statement on earlier lipid lowering, AHA statement on PAD in acute care, UKKA guideline on AF anticoagulation in advanced CKD, AST IDCOP peritransplant infection update.

top.title: Incretin-based obesity trials: ribupatide (GEMINI-1, JAMA) and lower-dose CagriSema (REDEFINE 9)
bullets: Mechanism (ribupatide): dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, once weekly subcutaneous.
GEMINI-1: 567 adults in China without diabetes; weight change at 48 weeks -10.7%, -16.4%, -17.7% with 2, 4, 6 mg vs -1.4% placebo; placebo-adjusted -9.3, -15.0, -16.3 percentage points.
REDEFINE 9: 309 adults without diabetes, mean BMI 39.1; weight change at 68 weeks -20.7% (1.7 mg each) and -21.0% (1.0 mg each) vs -2.0% pooled placebo (efficacy estimand).
At least 5% weight loss: 85.7% to 88.0% with ribupatide 4 to 6 mg vs 16.0%; 95.1% and 96.3% with CagriSema vs 33.4%.
top.caveat: REDEFINE 9 funded by Novo Nordisk; GEMINI-1 limited to adults in China with mean age 34.4 years; gastrointestinal adverse events 47.9% to 63.1% with ribupatide vs 23.1%; no outcome data.

top.title: Finerenone in focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FIND-CKD prespecified analysis, JASN)
bullets: 215 participants with FSGS (half primary, half secondary), mean eGFR 45, median UPCR 1427 mg/g, on stable RAS inhibition.
Total eGFR slope improved by 1.3 mL/min/1.73 m2/yr vs placebo (95% CI 0.5-2.2); consistent in biopsy-proven FSGS (1.4) and in primary vs secondary disease.
UPCR down 41% at month 12; kidney composite HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.30-1.15).
Hyperkalemia-related adverse events 15% vs 20%.
top.caveat: Subgroup of a larger nondiabetic CKD trial; composite end point not significant; proteomics analysis post hoc.

top.title: Coronary physiology and lesion preparation: LIPSIA-STRATEGY and VICTORY (JACC)
bullets: LIPSIA-STRATEGY: 1053 patients with intermediate stenoses; 1-year MACE 3.0% with angiography-derived vFFR vs 4.1% with wire FFR (risk difference -1.01 percentage points; P for noninferiority <0.001).
vFFR led to more revascularization of the study lesion (41.2% vs 35.5%).

VICTORY: 278 patients with calcified lesions; stent expansion 85% with super-high-pressure noncompliant balloons vs 84% with intravascular lithotripsy (P noninferiority <0.0001); 30-day TVF 2.8% vs 5.7% (HR 0.50; 95% CI 0.15-1.66).
top.caveat: LIPSIA event rate lower than anticipated; post hoc relative-margin sensitivity analysis failed noninferiority in mITT. VICTORY uses an imaging surrogate end point, experienced operators with mandatory OCT, 30-day clinical follow-up.

guidelines.title: Lipid-lowering strategies in the era of early atherosclerosis detection
bullets: Supports earlier identification and more sustained treatment based on lifetime LDL-C burden, inherited and acquired risk enhancers, and subclinical atherosclerosis imaging.
Imaging-detected atherosclerosis may identify people whose risk calculators underestimate.
Direct evidence in younger, low short-term-risk populations remains limited; screening strategy, thresholds and cost-effectiveness flagged as open questions.

guidelines.title: Peripheral artery disease in acute care settings
bullets: Covers PAD as a comorbidity in patients hospitalized for other cardiovascular or medical conditions.
Vascular access for acute MI, cardiogenic shock and valve procedures, mechanical circulatory support placement, and management after recent endovascular or surgical intervention.

guidelines.issuer: UK Kidney Association (endorsed by British Cardiovascular Society)
guidelines.title: Anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation in adults with advanced kidney disease
bullets: Addresses CrCl below 30 mL/min and dialysis, populations excluded from DOAC trials.
Recommendations on no anticoagulation as an option, DOAC use, anticoagulant monitoring and left atrial appendage occlusion; abstract does not state the individual recommendations.

guidelines.issuer: American Society of Transplantation Infectious Diseases Community of Practice
guidelines.title: Pretransplant and peritransplant infections (update of 2019 guidance)
bullets: Donor and recipient screening, donor-derived infection, pretransplant VAD infection, perioperative prophylaxis.
Posttransplant intra-abdominal infection, pneumonia, UTI and diarrhea; modified GRADE; part of a 5-article series.

guidelines.title: Revised clinical trial response criteria for invasive fungal disease (5-paper series)
bullets: Updates the 2008 MSG/EORTC response criteria for aspergillosis and other molds, invasive candidiasis, cryptococcosis and endemic mycoses in adults and children.
Cryptococcal meningitis phase 3 trials: 2-week mortality as primary end point; 10-week or longer survival and CSF clearance as secondary; early fungicidal activity for phase 2 (PMID 43043174).
Companion papers: molds (43043132), candidiasis (43043134), endemic mycoses (43043169).

guidelines.title: 2026-2027 influenza, RSV and SARS-CoV-2 immunization for nonpregnant, immunocompetent adults and health care personnel
bullets: Applies to adults 19 years and older; follows the AAFP Adult Immunization Schedule, reviewed annually.
Abstract states AAFP guidance should be followed where it differs from other organizations; specific recommendations not given in the abstract.

guidelines.title: Role of liver biopsy
bullets: Evidence and best practice for liver biopsy in liver disease, abnormal liver tests and liver masses.
Expert commentary format; abstract lists no specific advice statements.

guidelines.title: ACR Appropriateness Criteria: chronic liver disease, 2026 update
bullets: Imaging selection for hemochromatosis, steatosis and fibrosis assessment and surveillance.
RAND/UCLA method and GRADE; expert opinion where evidence is lacking.

guidelines.title: Initiation and interruption of kidney replacement therapy in acute kidney injury
bullets: Favors an individualized, dynamic decision over fixed early or delayed initiation.
Weaning predictors: urine output above 400 mL/day without diuretics or above 2000 mL/day with diuretics, creatinine clearance above 15 mL/min, no electrolyte or acid-base disturbance.

guidelines.issuer: Chinese Society of Clinical Pharmacy / Chinese Society of Renal Diseases
guidelines.title: Diagnosis, treatment and management of drug-induced kidney injury (2026)
bullets: Definition, classification, causative drugs, risk factors, severity assessment, prevention, treatment and follow-up.
Risk identification workflows, monitoring frequency and referral criteria aimed at primary care; Chinese-language full text.

guidelines.issuer: SED / SEEN / SEMERGEN / SEMFyC / SEMG (Spain, consensus)
guidelines.title: Continuous glucose monitoring in type 2 diabetes on basal insulin
bullets: Priority indications, glycemic targets, follow-up and discontinuation criteria for CGM.
Abstract does not list the specific indications.

guidelines.title: Genetic testing pathway for cardiomyopathies after the 2023 ESC guidelines
bullets: Builds on the ESC Class I, level B recommendation for genetic testing in cardiomyopathy.
Covers phenotype-first approach, testing strategy, direct-to-consumer testing, VUS interpretation, ACMG-based variant reclassification and reproductive counselling.

guidelines.title: Obesity prevention and care
bullets: Frames obesity as a chronic disease; current prevention measures judged inadequate.
Priorities: food and activity environment, stigma, care delivery models, access to medication and surgery, long-term adherence, payment reform.

items.title: Angiography-derived vFFR vs wire FFR to guide revascularization (LIPSIA-STRATEGY)
bullets: n=1053, intermediate stenoses, acute or chronic coronary syndromes, 8 German centers.
1-year MACE 3.0% vs 4.1% (relative risk 0.75; 95% CI 0.39-1.45); upper 1-sided 97.5% CI 1.29 percentage points vs 3.5 margin.
Physiological value 0.80 or less in 43.1% vs 35.9%; study lesion revascularized 41.2% vs 35.5%.
items.caveat: Low event rate made the absolute margin lenient; post hoc relative-margin analysis failed noninferiority in mITT, passed per protocol. Investigator-initiated.

items.title: Super-high-pressure noncompliant balloons vs intravascular lithotripsy in calcified lesions (VICTORY)
bullets: n=278; 68% severe calcium (OCT Fujino score 4 or more); median pressure 40 vs 6 atm.
OCT stent expansion 85% vs 84% (P noninferiority <0.0001); consistent across calcium severity.
30-day TVF 2.8% vs 5.7% (HR 0.50; 95% CI 0.15-1.66); perforation rates did not differ.
items.caveat: Imaging surrogate primary end point; open-label; experienced operators; 30-day clinical follow-up only.

items.title: Initial CTO-PCI vs no CTO-PCI (DECISION-CTO, 10 years)
bullets: n=804 mITT, 19 centers in 5 Asian countries; 10-year follow-up complete in 85.6%.
Death, MI, stroke or any revascularization 33.9% vs 37.4% (risk difference -3.5 percentage points; 95% CI -10.4 to 3.3).
items.caveat: Open-label; wide CIs; PCI of non-CTO lesions encouraged in both arms.

items.title: Biatrial vs left atrial maze during rheumatic mitral valve surgery (ABLATION)
bullets: n=323 with persistent or long-standing persistent AF; mean LA diameter 51.9 mm.
Freedom from atrial tachyarrhythmia off antiarrhythmics at 12 months 78.7% vs 68.6% (adjusted difference 10.7%; P=0.01).
Freedom from permanent pacemaker 97.0% vs 98.1%, noninferior (margin -5%).
items.caveat: Rheumatic mitral disease only; 12-month follow-up; generalizability to degenerative valve disease uncertain.

items.title: Dedicated transcatheter valve (Trilogy) for aortic regurgitation in LVAD patients (JENA-VAD)
bullets: n=50; technical and device success 96.0%; freedom from VARC-3 early safety composite events 90.0%.
No early death, stroke or MI; new pacemaker in 1 of 7 without prior pacing.
Leaflet thickening or thrombosis in 11 of 12 imaged patients (22% of cohort, a lower bound).
items.caveat: Uncontrolled; median follow-up 105 days; 38 of 50 had no postprocedure imaging.

items.design: Diagnostic and prognostic model development, external validation
items.title: AI-ECG for detection and prediction of dilated cardiomyopathy
bullets: Trained on more than 330 000 ECG-echocardiogram pairs; validated in UK Biobank, Zhongshan and Antwerp cohorts.
AUC .87-.97 for prevalent DCM phenotype; C-index .80-.87 for future DCM, comparable to echocardiography (.80-.90).
Familial cascade-screening cohorts: 5-year NPV 95.5% and 91.5%, PPV 42.4% and 39.4%; high-risk score 5.1-6.4-fold higher incident DCM.
items.caveat: Familial cohorts small (n=166 and 177); retrospective; no evidence yet that surveillance guided by the model changes outcomes.

items.title: Long-term cause-specific mortality after acute pulmonary embolism (China)
bullets: n=66 192 from 3223 chest pain centres, 2018-2023.
5-year all-cause mortality 22.41%: cardiovascular 11.84%, non-cardiovascular 10.57%.
Ischaemic heart disease the largest named cause after 12 months; malignancy peaked at 1-3 months.
Mortality 11.52% under 55 years vs 38.51% at 75 or older.
items.caveat: Observational; cause of death from registry linkage; associated-factor analyses exploratory.

items.title: Once-weekly ribupatide for weight loss in adults in China (GEMINI-1)
bullets: Mechanism: dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist.
n=567 without diabetes; mean BMI 33.3; 48 weeks.
Weight change -10.7%, -16.4%, -17.7% (2, 4, 6 mg) vs -1.4%; placebo-adjusted -9.3, -15.0, -16.3 percentage points.
Gastrointestinal adverse events 47.9% to 63.1% vs 23.1%; 0.7% discontinued for adverse events.
items.caveat: Chinese population, young (mean age 34.4); no cardiometabolic outcome data.

items.title: Cagrilintide-semaglutide 1.7 mg each and 1.0 mg each (REDEFINE 9)
bullets: n=309 without diabetes, mean BMI 39.1, 77% female; 68 weeks.
Weight change -20.7% (1.7 mg each) and -21.0% (1.0 mg each) vs -2.0% pooled placebo; ETD -18.8 and -19.0 percentage points.
At least 5% loss: 95.1% and 96.3% vs 33.4%.
Adverse events 99% and 95% vs 91%, mostly gastrointestinal, mild or moderate.
items.caveat: Funded by Novo Nordisk; efficacy estimand reported; 82% on treatment at week 68.

items.title: Acupoint thread embedding for weight loss in women (Ann Intern Med)
bullets: n=132 women aged 18 to 45, BMI 24 or higher; 6 sessions over 12 weeks.
BMI -0.7 kg/m2 and weight -1.8 kg vs sham at week 12; -1.1 kg/m2 and -3.0 kg at week 24.
At least 5% weight loss 25.8% vs 9.1% at 12 weeks; cardiometabolic outcomes did not differ.
items.caveat: Single center in Shanghai; acupuncturists unmasked; modest effect; short follow-up.

items.title: Diabetes-educated psychologist added to care in type 1 diabetes with HbA1c above 7.8%
bullets: n=151, mean HbA1c 9.2%, 6 Swedish clinics; median 9 counseling sessions; 52 weeks.
Diabetes distress reduced (difference -0.2; P=0.040) and treatment satisfaction improved (3.5; P=0.004).
items.caveat: Open-label; small; secondary outcomes positive but primary not met.

items.title: Denosumab for osteoporosis beyond 10 years
bullets: 4030 treated; 400 with 10 years or more cumulative exposure vs 350 with 5 to 10 years.
BMD rose steadily without plateau beyond 10 years.
18 ONJ and 2 AFF cases across the whole cohort, without temporal relation to duration.
items.caveat: Single-center real-world chart review; surrogate BMD end point; no fracture outcomes in abstract.

items.title: LC-MS/MS plasma steroid profiling to separate Cushing's disease from ectopic ACTH
bullets: 128 patients (95 CD, 33 EAS) at Peking Union Medical College Hospital.
Predictors: androstenedione (root node), LC-MS/MS cortisol, age, sex.
Apparent AUC 0.986; accuracy 96.9% (124/128).
items.caveat: Apparent performance in development cohort only; needs external validation before replacing BIPSS.

items.title: Finerenone in FSGS (FIND-CKD)
bullets: n=215 of 1584; mean eGFR 45, median UPCR 1427 mg/g.
Total eGFR slope +1.3 mL/min/1.73 m2/yr vs placebo (95% CI 0.5-2.2; P=0.002).
UPCR -41% at month 12; UPCR below 700 mg/g OR 6.8; kidney composite HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.30-1.15).
Hyperkalemia-related adverse events 15% vs 20%.
items.caveat: Subgroup of a nondiabetic CKD trial; composite underpowered.

items.title: GFR slope as a surrogate when eGFR falls by a non-glomerular mechanism (FIELD, fenofibrate)
bullets: n=9795, 5 years; fenofibrate acute eGFR decline -9.05 mL/min/1.73 m2.
Chronic slope better (+0.61) but total slope worse (-1.54); clinical kidney composite HR 1.48 (95% CI 1.16-1.89).
Post-washout eGFR (n=660) showed benefit on total slope, contrary to on-study analysis.
items.caveat: Methodological; creatinine-based end points can diverge from measured kidney function for drugs that alter creatinine handling.

items.title: Dietary sodium restriction and acute endothelin-A receptor antagonism in proteinuric CKD
bullets: Mechanism: BQ123, selective endothelin-A receptor antagonist (intravenous).
n=12 non-diabetic proteinuric CKD on maximal RAAS inhibition; 13.3 vs 6.3 g salt/day.
Systolic BP fell about 12-14 mmHg under both diets.
GFR (about 5 mL/min/1.73 m2), filtration fraction and proteinuria (about 300 ug/min) fell only with sodium restriction.
items.caveat: Very small; acute infusion; tool compound, not a marketed ERA; long-term relevance untested.

items.title: Ammonia predicts hospitalization for bacterial infection in outpatients with cirrhosis
bullets: n=1855 from 5 European and 1 Singaporean centres; 8% of European patients developed infection within 1 year.
Ammonia 1.75 vs 0.97 times ULN in those infected; each unit raised risk 12-14%; 1.4 times ULN threshold identified higher infection and OHE risk.
C-index for infection 0.725 (Europe) and 0.877 (Singapore); AMMON-OHE 0.805.
items.caveat: Retrospective; association, not causation; ammonia sampling standards vary across centres.

items.title: Upadacitinib in Takayasu arteritis (SELECT-TAK)
bullets: Mechanism: oral JAK inhibitor.
n=59 with prior failed glucocorticoid taper; 15 mg daily vs placebo with standardized taper.
Time to first relapse HR 0.52 (95% CI 0.24-1.12); primary end point not met despite log-rank p=0.045.
Relapse 37% vs 62%; median time to relapse 107.9 vs 20.1 weeks; serious adverse events 9 vs 4.
items.caveat: Funded by AbbVie; small; 61% Japanese.

items.title: Prediction-aided bDMARD tapering in RA (PATIO)
bullets: n=162 with sustained low disease activity; 18 months.
Flares per patient 1.00 vs 0.73 with disease activity-guided tapering alone (rate ratio 1.32; 95% CI 0.90-1.95).
Any flare 57% vs 44%; major flares 22% vs 15%; dose reduction similar.
Tapering advice not followed at 23% of visits.
items.caveat: Superiority trial; point estimates favor usual tapering; adherence to model advice incomplete.

items.title: High-risk medication prescribing in older adults with rheumatic disease
bullets: n=45 455 aged 65 or older; 30.7% received at least 1 high-risk medication.
82.3% of prescriptions from non-rheumatology clinicians; muscle relaxants, first-generation antihistamines, anticholinergic antidepressants, Z-drugs common.
Highest odds in axial SpA (OR 1.40) and Sjogren's disease (OR 1.39) vs RA.
items.caveat: Cross-sectional, 2021 data; no outcome linkage.

items.title: Genetic risk scores and b/tsDMARD treatment patterns in RA
bullets: 2454 (MVP) and 461 (MGB) patients; patterns: TNFi persisters, TNFi to abatacept, multi-drug cyclers.
Higher RA GRS: multi-drug cycling OR 1.137 per SD vs TNFi persisters.
Higher SpA GRS: lower odds of cycling (OR 0.824), i.e. more TNFi persistence.
items.caveat: Small effect sizes; not a predictive tool yet; mostly veteran cohort.

items.title: GLP-1-based drugs vs tezepelumab in obesity-associated asthma without diabetes
bullets: Mechanism: GLP-1 receptor agonists and dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists, compared with tezepelumab.
n=2779 (semaglutide 1770, tirzepatide 472, liraglutide 133, tezepelumab 404) with at least 1 severe exacerbation in the prior year.
Severe exacerbation vs tezepelumab: tirzepatide wHR 0.41 (95% CI 0.24-0.70); semaglutide wHR 0.99 (0.70-1.39).
items.caveat: Observational, confounding by indication; authors call for trials.

items.title: Telemedicine-based vs in-person APAP management in OSA: 24-hour blood pressure
bullets: n=344 randomized, 256 completed 3 months.
Difference in 24-hour mean BP change -0.59 mmHg (95% CI -2.42 to 1.25) ITT; upper limit below 1.5 mmHg margin.
No clear difference in APAP adherence, patient-reported or metabolic outcomes.
items.caveat: 26% did not complete follow-up; 3 months only.

items.title: Mortality in invasive aspergillosis
bullets: IPD from 46 studies, 3880 patients (209 eligible studies, 15 357 patients).
Mortality 26.7% at 4 weeks, 41.7% at 12 weeks, 53.8% at 1 year, 57.2% at 2 years.
ICU mortality 57.1%; 4-week mortality 42.9% with ICU admission and 40.4% for brain disease.
items.caveat: I2 above 89%; IPD obtained for a minority of eligible studies; COVID-19 dominated the ICU cohort.

items.title: High-dose vs standard-dose influenza vaccine: symptom burden in breakthrough infection (DANFLU-2 Homeswab)
bullets: 10 140 randomized aged 65 or older; 1273 analyzable self-swabs, 121 influenza-positive (44 vs 77).
Symptom severity in laboratory-confirmed influenza did not differ.
Post hoc relative vaccine effectiveness against confirmed influenza 42.2% (95% CI 16.4%-60.0%).
items.caveat: Exploratory; few breakthrough infections; incomplete questionnaire completion.

items.title: Rifampicin exposure and tolerability in high-dose TB preventive therapy (2R2)
bullets: n=1368 adults and adolescents; 2 months at 20 or 30 mg/kg/day vs 4 months at 10 mg/kg/day.
Doubling of AUC0-24: AE-related discontinuation aOR 1.88; non-AE discontinuation aOR 1.42; tolerability symptoms aOR 1.48.
No significant association with hepatotoxicity.
items.caveat: Exposure modeled from 440 sampled participants; efficacy not assessed.

items.title: Physiotherapist telephone coaching vs text messaging for adults with mobility limitations (ComeBACK, BMJ)
bullets: n=512, mean age 69, 76% women, 5 Australian states.
Daily steps at 6 months +931 vs waitlist (95% CI 409-1452) and +571 vs texting.
Texting vs waitlist +359 (not significant); no serious adverse events.
items.caveat: Participants and coaches unmasked; device-measured steps as surrogate; 6-month primary time point.

method: Source: PubMed E-utilities, entry date within the last 7 days. Query A: 30 internal medicine and subspecialty journals. Query B: publication type Practice Guideline or Guideline in internal medicine topics. Duplicates removed by PMID.
Screening and summaries: Claude, from abstracts and metadata only. Numbers are copied from abstracts; open the linked record before citing.
Full text: PMC records exist for 14 of 139 candidates. A PMC record does not guarantee machine-readable full text.

Excluded by scope: oncology (including BCMA CAR-T and myeloma trials, FORTE, breast irradiation, French prostate cancer guideline), neurology (tau biomarkers, dementia), pediatrics (semaglutide in children, SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS, youth-onset type 1 diabetes food insecurity, Swiss paediatric home respiratory support, Powassan virus in children), obstetrics and gynecology (menopause, gestational diabetes, intrapartum trial, prenatal cfDNA), surgery-only (cardiac surgery delirium consensus, robotic pancreatoduodenectomy), ISHLT transplant nursing workforce statement, health policy, narrative and opinion pieces. R21/Matrix-M seasonal malaria mass vaccination trial (Lancet) skipped as a community vaccination campaign outside the internal medicine scope.
Not searched: preprints, society websites without PubMed indexing (ACC, ESC, KDIGO, IDSA, ADA living updates), FDA actions.
Badges describe the result against the primary end point: Positive, Negative, Neutral (no clear difference), Descriptive (observational, uncontrolled, or no efficacy test).
